highlights.description: Organizations without a plan: a first social login creates the person's personal organization, slugs are reserved, renamed with a cooling-off period and aliases, a personal organization converts to a team, and what an organization may use comes from its marketplace subscriptions and licenses (ADR-006)
Application roles per member, entitled through the marketplace, carried in the `orgs` claim and on invites, with relying parties reading memberships from claims by default (ADR-007)

Real-time invalidation of access: access tokens default to 10 minutes and are capped at 15, every access-reducing change is recorded, and relying parties refuse tokens issued before it, with polling, replay and back-channel delivery (ADR-010)

Resource-scoped collaborators: the `collaborator` organization role, resource grants with a standard viewer, contributor and maintainer ladder in both authorization modes, and invites that target one resource (ADR-008)
The authorization mode is configuration: the `authz` key selects `rbac` or `rebac`, and `authz/mode.New` builds the provider, syncer and grant store (ADR-008)

Management is derived from manager relationships; a manager can release a principal, a self-managed human can be invited to be managed or decline, and managing operations are authorized and served over HTTP (ADR-009)
Editor and viewer are no longer organization roles, and the organization `plan` column is removed; run migrations 0004 to 0009 on existing PostgreSQL databases

breaking.description: The organization `plan` column and `organization.Plan` constants are removed from the schema, service inputs, list filter, API and SCIM group provisioning; organization responses carry an `entitlements` list instead. Existing PostgreSQL databases run migrations/0004_drop_organization_plan.sql

`editor` and `viewer` are no longer organization roles: the roles are owner, admin, member and collaborator, every membership path refuses any other value, and the base schema gains the `collaborator` relation and `list` permission. migrations/0008_drop_editor_viewer_roles.sql maps stored `editor` to `member` and `viewer` to `collaborator`, including pending invites
Every path that creates or changes a membership validates the role against owner, admin, member and collaborator and answers ErrInvalidRole otherwise

The marketplace SpiceDB fragment no longer redefines `principal` and `organization`; it attaches to the base organization through a `marketplace_org` facet carrying use, billing and purchase. Compose it with MergeSchema, which places the base schema first

Entitlement checks fail closed: an approle service with no entitlement source entitles no organization to any application. Configure marketplace.EntitlementSource through marketplace.ApproleOptions, or use approle.EntitleAll in development and tests

Relying parties read memberships from SystemAuth claims by default (ClaimsMemberships); LocalMemberships is no longer picked up implicitly from the principal store and is for development and tests only
The default access token lifetime drops from 15 to 10 minutes, and a configured lifetime above 15 minutes is refused at load; per-client lifetimes are capped at 15 minutes

upgradeGuide.description: Run the migrations against an existing PostgreSQL database, in order: 0004_drop_organization_plan, 0005_subscriptions_per_listing, 0006_invite_app_roles, 0007_oauth_app_backchannel_logout_uri, 0008_drop_editor_viewer_roles and 0009_invite_resource_target. Each is idempotent. Fresh databases need none of them. Then run `systemauth migrate` for the new tables sf_app_roles, sf_slug_reservations, sf_access_changes, sf_resource_grants and sf_manager_invites

Replace uses of the organization plan with entitlements: remove `Plan` from organization inputs and filters, and read `entitlements` from organization responses. Supply APIConfig.Entitlements with marketplace.EntitlementSource; carry a paid tier over as a subscription or license

Replace `editor` and `viewer` in your own role tables, vocabularies and invites with `member` and `collaborator` (or resource roles); stored memberships are mapped by migration 0008, which records an access change for each active membership it changes

Configure entitlements for application roles: build the approle service with marketplace.ApproleOptions(marketplace.EntitlementSource(...)), and declare applications free to everyone with marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements. Without them no organization is entitled to anything, and marketplace.WarnIfNoEntitlements logs a startup warning

Relying parties that depended on LocalMemberships must pass it explicitly. The default reads the `orgs` claim; use ClaimsOrRemoteMemberships to fall back to /oauth/userinfo/memberships when the claim is truncated or absent

Pass a revocation cache to BearerMiddleware and NewBFF to refuse tokens issued before an access change; feed it with accesschange.ToSink in one process, the poller across replicas, or back-channel delivery across deployments. Review any configured access_token_lifetime against the 15 minute cap

Build the authorization provider from configuration with `authz/mode.New(ctx, cfg.Authz, mode.Deps{...})` and pass its Syncer to the identity services. The `authz` key defaults to `rbac`. The `authz/simple` and `authz/spicedb` forwarding packages remain deprecated and will be removed in the next major release; import `authz/rbac` and `authz/rebac/spicedb`

When switching to `rebac`, write existing memberships, application roles and resource grants into the graph through the syncer before serving requests, and write the composed schema (embedded instances always receive it; remote ones only with `write_schema`)

added.description: A first GitHub or Google login creates the person's personal organization and owner membership in the same transaction as the principal, and an existing principal without one gets it on its next login; the slug is the GitHub username or the email local part, with a numeric suffix on collision (ADR-006). signup.SlugForLogin, signup.CreatePersonalOrgInTx and signup.EnsurePersonalOrgInTx expose the derivation and the in-transaction creation

Reserved slugs: organization.ReservedSlugs lists names no organization may take, WithReservedSlugs adds product names, and signup avoids them; a managed principal's slug is a manager-entered value or a generated adjective-noun-NN, never its email (signup.SlugForManaged)

Personal organization rules: a personal organization has one member, its owner, and refuses members, invitations, SCIM membership and ownership transfer with ErrPersonalOrganization unless the role is collaborator
Slug rename with a cooling-off period (default 7 days, WithSlugCoolingOff), reservations in sf_slug_reservations, and aliases through ResolveSlug so old links keep working
organization.ConvertToTeam turns a personal organization into a team in one transaction and creates a new personal organization under the handle

Entitlements derived from the marketplace: organization responses carry an `entitlements` list built from active subscriptions, valid licenses and default entitlements, and subscriptions may be per listing (migration 0005)

Entitled applications: a listing may name an application, and marketplace.ApproleOptions maps subscriptions, licenses and marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements to applications with seat limits from seat-based licenses

Application roles: the AppRole schema (sf_app_roles) and the approle service to assign, change and remove a role per principal, organization and application, with endpoints under /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles
Application roles reach the authorization graph through the optional authz.AppRoleSyncer
The `orgs` claim in ID tokens, access tokens and userinfo, and a paginated GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships
relyingparty membership sources: ClaimsMemberships, RemoteMemberships, ClaimsOrRemoteMemberships and ProvisioningMemberships
Invitations carry application roles to grant on acceptance, validated against entitlements and seats (migration 0006)
sf_access_changes and the accesschange package record every access-reducing change in the transaction that makes it and announce it to a sink
Access changes are recorded for member removal and deactivation, organization and application role changes, ownership transfer, principal deactivation and session or token revocation
relyingparty.RevocationCache, and BearerMiddleware and the BFF refuse tokens issued before an access change, after a clock-skew margin
Access-change poller, replay after a restart, suspect-start mode and the GET /access-changes endpoint with the access_changes:read scope

Back-channel delivery of access changes as OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout tokens to clients that register backchannel_logout_uri (migration 0007), and relyingparty.BackchannelHandler to receive them
Access-change reasons form an open, validated registry
The resource-role ladder (viewer, contributor, maintainer) and the ResourceGranter contract
Resource grants stored in sf_resource_grants and mirrored to the graph; the role-based provider consults and manages them
The relationship-based provider writes grants as relationships and lists resources by lookup, and vocabulary fragments validate collaborator-able definitions
Resource-targeted invites: an invite can name a resource type, id and role, and accepting it creates the collaborator membership and the grant together (migration 0009)
The `authz` configuration key with `rbac` and `rebac` modes, ModeConfig and SpiceDBConfig
authz/mode.New builds the configured provider, relationship syncer and grant store from a ModeConfig, with Close
Management is derived from active manager relationships rather than from the absence of an email; a managed identity may carry an email
Release a principal from management, invite a self-managed human to be managed, and decline a manager invitation
A manager invitation can be declined by the invitee
Authorized managed-principal operations, deletion with erasure and an HTTP API for managing operations

changed.description: Unused stale Argon2id secret checkers are removed from the identity packages

deprecated.description: The `authz/simple` and `authz/spicedb` forwarding packages will be removed in the next major release; use `authz/rbac` and `authz/rebac/spicedb`

fixed.description: A login with no usable characters in its username gets a neutral slug
Accepting an invite syncs the new membership to the authorization graph
Principals and organizations created by social login are registered with the authorization syncer
Signup creates the principal and personal organization in one transaction
The application-role seat limit is checked under a lock so concurrent assignments cannot exceed it
A managed principal is never a valid manager
Authorization checks for AddManager, RemoveManager and Release run inside the row-locked transaction
Managing operations record the accurate access-change reason
The resource schema helper keeps `owner` and `delete`
Assigning an application role with no seat left answers 409 instead of 500

documentation.description: Architecture pages for organizations, managed principals and authorization describe the implemented behavior
Guides for invites, application roles and entitlements, collaborators and resource grants, organization slugs, personal-to-team conversion, access-change invalidation and the authorization mode
Feature specifications moved from docs/design to docs/specs
INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-011 specifications for the organizations initiative

tests.description: The test person-server client uses an explicit HTTP client

highlights.description: Managed principals: humans without an email, such as young learners, created and controlled by guardian and educator managers, who sign them in with QR-friendly login tokens; opt-in per deployment and per client (ADR-005)

Principal is the sole identity root: the legacy User model and its dependent tables are removed, so password login, social login, federation sync, and SCIM all resolve a person to the same principal (ADR-004)
Resource servers can authenticate AI agents with AAuth through a protocol-neutral request principal and authenticator chain shared with bearer, API-key, and BFF-session credentials
Fixed a panic on every ascending SCIM list sort, including the default order
Security: the marketplace, organization, and invite APIs act for the authenticated caller and check organization permissions, instead of trusting IDs in the request; invite tokens are stored hashed
The simple and SpiceDB authorization providers grant the same organization and manager permissions, held to the base schema by a parity test and a shared conformance suite

breaking.description: Removed Ent schemas and packages user, membership, oauthaccount, refreshtoken, apikey, serviceaccount, and serviceaccountkeypair, with the Organization memberships, api_keys, and service_accounts edges and OAuthToken.service_account_id

systemauth.Storage user methods are replaced by CreateHuman, GetHuman, GetHumanByEmail, GetHumanByExternalIdentity, LinkExternalIdentity, UpdateHuman, and DeleteHuman on one HumanPrincipal type; systemauth.User, LoginPrincipal, ErrUserNotFound, and ErrUserExists are removed in favor of HumanPrincipal, ErrPrincipalNotFound, and ErrPrincipalExists
OAuthApp.owner references Principal; statically configured clients are owned by a service principal at the fixed system ID instead of a synthetic user
OAuth tokens and authorization codes drop user_id and the user edge in favor of the subject column; OAuthConsent.user_id becomes principal_id
SCIM users are human principals and group membership uses PrincipalMembership; users provisioned before this release are not visible through SCIM
An existing PostgreSQL development database must run migrations/0002_drop_legacy_user_tables.sql before starting this version; fresh databases need no migration
The default BFF session cookie is sf_session instead of the Core-era cf_session; browsers holding the old cookie sign in again. Applications that set CookieConfig.Name are unaffected
organization.Service ListMembers and ListMemberships exclude inactive memberships unless IncludeInactive is passed, and take variadic ListOption arguments
mixin.UserBase and mixin.MembershipBase are removed

Human.email is optional: a human without one is a managed principal with the identifier human:<id>. HumanPrincipal.Email, principal.Human.Email, and contract identity types treat it as optional; existing creation paths still require an email

Marketplace checkout buys as the authenticated caller for an organization the caller may buy for, and answers 501 until marketplace.WithPurchaseAuthorizer or WithAuthorizer is configured; purchaser_id is optional, deprecated, and must equal the caller

Marketplace listing and license operations answer 501 until marketplace.WithAuthorizer is configured and require an authenticated caller; only published listings are readable anonymously; owner_id and assigned_by are optional, deprecated, and must equal the caller
Organization API endpoints require an authenticated caller and, except creating an organization and checking a slug, answer 501 until APIConfig.Authorizer is set

Invite API endpoints require an authenticated caller and organization endpoints answer 501 until APIConfig.Authorizer is set; accepting and declining require the invite to be addressed to the caller's email; inviter_principal_id, principal_id, and the email query are optional, deprecated, and must match the caller

Invite tokens are stored hashed and invite.Invite no longer has a Token field; the token is only in InviteResult.InviteURL. Existing PostgreSQL databases run migrations/0003_hash_invite_tokens.sql when deploying
spicedb.BaseSchema is now authz.BaseSpiceDBSchema: members hold contribute rather than edit on an organization, and editors are recognized

authz.RelationshipSyncer gains AddPrincipalManager and RemovePrincipalManager; credential.Service gains IssueLoginToken and VerifyLoginToken; managedprincipal.Gate implementers also provide LoginTokenPolicy
identity/token reports typed errors (ErrInvalidAccessToken, ErrInvalidRefreshToken, ErrRefreshTokenReused, ErrDPoPMismatch, ErrScopeNotGranted)
marketplace.LicenseService gains GetByStripeSubscriptionID; Stripe webhook endpoints should also subscribe to checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded

delegation errors are typed and an agent without a delegation is denied; signup's SignupOrGetExisting requires SignupInput.EmailVerified to return an existing account, and SignupWithInvite requires the invited email

systemauth.WithUserIDHeader is removed; use WithTrustedUserIDHeader with a RequestGate (TrustedProxyNetworks or TrustAllRequests), social login, or your own SessionProvider. DefaultSessionProvider authenticates nobody by default
identity/oauth's authorization endpoint refuses requests until WithUserAuthenticator or WithTrustedUserIDHeader is set, and third-party clients are refused until WithConsent is set

session/ratelimit: IPKey and the Limiter default no longer read X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP (use ForwardedIPKey or ForwardedClientIP behind proxies), the middleware answers 503 on storage errors unless WithFailOpen is given, and MemoryStorage returns ErrTooManyKeys when full

session/bff: TrustProxy and TrustCloudflare do nothing without TrustedProxies or CloudflareIPRanges; session/middleware no longer reads forwarding headers for API key usage addresses unless an IPExtractor is given
scim: a provider without WithAuthorizationHook answers 403 to every request; DefaultAuthorizationHook is deprecated for AllowAllAuthorizationHook
systemauth: NewFederationEndpoints registers the sync and lookup routes only with WithFederationAuthenticator; introspection callers need a confidential client or the introspect scope

session/jwt and contract: tokens without exp are refused, and jwt refuses another issuer when Config.Issuer is set; relyingparty.BearerMiddleware requires an allowed Origin and JSON body for cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, and DELETE
credential.ValidateClientSecret returns ErrInvalidClientCredentials for every rejection; multiapp.AppAwareDB.ForSchema returns an error

identity/apikey: Get, Revoke, and Delete take the owning principal and report other keys as not found; a service with no AllowedScopes grants no scopes unless AllowAnyScope is set; RevokeInOrganization added for organization administrators
rls: Helper.SetTenant and SetUser return ErrNotInTransaction for *sql.DB and *sql.Conn; Middleware.SetRLSContext no longer touches the database and Middleware.WithTx scopes a transaction

security.description: Marketplace checkout took the purchaser from the request body, so anyone could start a purchase in another principal's name for any organization
Marketplace listing, license, and seat endpoints acted on any IDs a request named; they now check the caller's permissions on the owning organization
The organization API listed every organization and let any caller read, change, or delete organizations, change members, and transfer ownership; it now authorizes each operation
Invite management needed no permission, and anyone holding an invite link could accept it as any principal; invites are now managed with invite_member and accepted only by the addressee
Invite tokens were stored in plain text, so a leaked table or backup could accept invites; they are stored as SHA-256 hashes
SpiceDB principal and organization cleanup ignored failures and missed editor and manager relations, leaving access behind while reporting success

Refresh-token rotation was not atomic and its revocation error was discarded, so a refresh token could be used more than once; refreshing near expiry also reset a session to seven days, extending it indefinitely. Rotation is now atomic, a family keeps its first expiry, and reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the family

Stripe checkout granted licenses for sessions completed with an unpaid delayed payment, a malformed seat count produced an unlimited seat-based license, and cancelled subscriptions kept their licenses

Deactivating a principal left its access tokens valid and let its refresh tokens keep issuing new ones for up to the family's absolute lifetime; SystemAuth and identity/token now refuse an inactive principal's tokens wherever they are used or refreshed, and revoke the family

Revoking an agent's delegation gave it unrestricted access, constraints that did not overlap allowed everything, and delegation expiry and action limits were never stored; delegation now fails closed and enforces every constraint
UpdateHuman granted or revoked platform administration without syncing it, so a revoked administrator stayed one in SpiceDB
SignupWithInvite let anyone holding an invite link join under any email, and SignupOrGetExisting returned an existing account for an unverified email

SystemAuth's default session provider and identity/oauth's authorization endpoint took the user from an X-User-ID request header, so anyone who could reach the endpoint could obtain an authorization code, and tokens, for any user; header identity is now an explicit, gated opt-in and the default authenticates nobody
identity/oauth granted every requested scope to every client without consent; non-first-party clients now need a consent check

SCIM listing and search never asked the authorization hook, so any caller with a token could dump every user and group, and the provider's default hook allowed everything; listings are authorized and the default denies

The federation identity sync endpoint trusted any well-formed request and acted on its body, letting an unauthenticated caller link to and then deactivate or rewrite any account by email; it and the lookup endpoint now require a FederationAuthenticator and are not registered without one

Rate limits keyed on client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP, so a client could evade a limit by rotating the header or poison a victim's; they key on the direct peer, and forwarded headers are believed only from configured trusted proxies, here and in the BFF client IP handling and the API key middleware

The in-memory rate-limit store grew without bound from attacker-chosen keys, the middleware failed open on storage errors, and the login token endpoint keyed on raw client_id values; the store is bounded, the middleware fails closed, and only registered clients get a bucket

Token introspection accepted any valid access token or any client's Basic credentials, public clients included, as the caller's credential; it now requires a confidential client or a token with the introspect scope
The default storage accepted every client-assertion JWT ID as new, so a captured private_key_jwt assertion could be replayed until it expired
BFF cookies lost Secure and HttpOnly when a CookieConfig omitted them; both are now unconditional unless AllowInsecure is set for development
Cookie-authenticated writes through relyingparty.BearerMiddleware skipped the same-origin check, allowing cross-site requests
JWT validation accepted tokens with no expiry and ignored the issuer; the contract middleware did the same and skipped the audience check without an app ID
Client secret validation revealed whether a client ID existed by error message and timing, and lockout counted differently spelled identifiers separately, restarting the count
multiapp's SchemaDB left a schema's search_path on pooled connections, which could carry one application's schema to unrelated code, and ForSchema interpolated unvalidated names into SQL
The BFF proxy forwarded the browser's session cookie upstream when a ProxyConfig was built by hand; Cookie, Authorization, and DPoP headers are now always stripped
multiapp trusted the X-App-ID header, so with a shared signing key a token for one app authenticated requests for another; MiddlewareConfig.AppAudiences binds tokens to the routed app
API keys could be read, revoked, or deleted by ID alone, requested any scope including the wildcard when no allow-list was set, and ignored MaxKeysPerUser
Lockout let a burst of parallel guesses exceed MaxAttempts; Lockout.Begin reserves the attempt before the credential is verified
Concurrent BFF refreshes spent one refresh token several times, which token reuse detection treats as theft; refresh is now serialized per session

added.description: identity/requestprincipal: a protocol-neutral RequestPrincipal, an Authenticator interface, and middleware that tries authenticators in order and challenges with every protocol when none recognizes the request
relyingparty.NewRequestAuthenticator adapts bearer authentication (SystemAuth access tokens, API keys, BFF sessions) to the request authenticator chain

identity/requestprincipal/aauthrs authenticates AI agents at resource servers with AAuth: message-signature and token verification, an issuer allowlist checked before key discovery, per-route scopes, and AAuth-Requirement challenges
migrations/0002 creates the system service principal, reassigns OAuth apps owned by legacy users, and drops the legacy tables and columns on existing PostgreSQL databases
A repository-wide test fails on references to the retired legacy identity model in code or current documentation
identity/clientassertion records used client-assertion JWT IDs in sf_client_assertion_jtis for replay protection
store.Config.TrustProvisionedEmail, off by default, marks emails written through SCIM as verified so social login can link to provisioned users
identity/pgschema applies PostgreSQL-only schema objects; the migrate step adds a unique index on lower(email) in sf_humans
The members endpoint accepts includeInactive to list deactivated memberships
identity/managedprincipal creates managed principals with their managers in one transaction, maintains manager relationships with a last-manager guard, and audits every action
ManagerRelationship (sf_manager_relationships) and ManagerClaim (sf_manager_claims) Ent schemas
Deployment managed_principals settings and the per-client managed_principals flag, both off by default, checked through Server.ManagedPrincipalsAllowed

login_token credentials: issued by a manager, hashed, verified in constant time, single-use option, with lifetimes from the request, the client's login_token_ttl, or the deployment default (30 days) under a ceiling (400 days); single-use tokens last 20 minutes
POST /login-token exchanges a login token for a SystemAuth login session, with identical responses for every failure and per-address and per-client rate limits (WithLoginTokenRateLimit)
ID token and userinfo claim managed: true for managed principals, and relying parties read it into VerifiedIdentity.Managed
Managers list and revoke a managed principal's login tokens, login sessions, and token families, individually or all at once, through managedprincipal.Service or NewHandler
Guardian claims: a manager issues a single-use code that makes a human with an email a guardian; AttachVerifiedEmail turns a managed principal into an ordinary human
Base schema relations guardian and educator on principal with manage_account, manage_credentials, view_profile, and manage_managers; authz.ManagerRolePermissions and simple.WithManagerRoleGetter
authz.OrgRolePermissions and the PermOrg* actions name the base organization permissions both providers evaluate
providertest.RunOrgPermissionTests and RunManagerRelationTests hold providers to the base schema's grants
marketplace.PurchaserChecker and stripe.WithPurchaserChecker refuse checkout to managed principals
marketplace.WithAuthorizer, WithPurchaseAuthorizer, OrgRolePurchaseAuthorizer, and WithCallerResolver configure how the marketplace API authorizes callers
organization.MembershipRoleGetter backs the simple provider with active memberships; APIConfig.Authorizer and Caller configure the organization and invite APIs
requestprincipal.PrincipalUUID resolves the caller's SystemForge principal ID
spicedb.Client.DeleteRelationships deletes relationships by filter
migrations/0003 converts stored invite tokens to hashes
CI runs the PostgreSQL tests against a database service and the SpiceDB provider tests with the integration tag; SF_TEST_PG_REQUIRED makes a missing database fail rather than skip
systemauth.PrincipalStatus lets storage report whether a token's principal is active; Ent and memory storage implement it
Agents store allowed actions, allowed scopes, and a delegation expiry
systemauth.RequestGate, TrustAllRequests, and TrustedProxyNetworks; oauth.WithUserAuthenticator, WithTrustedUserIDHeader, WithLoginURL, and WithConsent

jwt.ValidateAccessTokenForAudience and middleware.HTTPAuthForAudience; ratelimit.PeerIP, ForwardedClientIP, ForwardedIPKey, WithMaxKeys, WithFailOpen; systemauth.WithLoginTokenClientIP, FederationAuthenticator, SharedSecretAuthenticator, and AuthorizeIntrospectionCaller; scim.DenyAllAuthorizationHook
session/jwt: TokenOptions.Audience addresses one token to its own audience
multiapp: MiddlewareConfig.AppAudiences binds tokens to the app a request is routed to
identity/security: Lockout.Begin and Attempt reserve a login attempt before verification

changed.description: `authz` providers are named for their mode: role-based `authz/rbac` (formerly `authz/simple`) and relationship-based `authz/rebac/spicedb` (formerly `authz/spicedb`), so another engine can sit beside SpiceDB under the same mode
Federation sync records the federation identity as an ExternalIdentity; creating an identity for an existing email links it so later updates and deletes resolve to the same principal
Human email uniqueness is enforced case-insensitively on create and update in SystemAuth and SCIM, matching the case-insensitive lookups
SCIM userName is not case-exact (RFC 7643): lookups, uniqueness, and eq and co filters ignore case
SCIM memberships honor the active flag, and deleting a user who belongs to a group removes the memberships instead of failing
Creating an organization through the API makes the caller its owner, and every organization with an owner gives it an owner membership
Listing organizations returns the caller's organizations, or all of them for platform administrators
SCIM no longer lists, reads, changes, deletes, or groups managed principals
Signup requires a bare email address

deprecated.description: `authz/simple` and `authz/spicedb` forward to `authz/rbac` and `authz/rebac/spicedb` as deprecated packages for one release; importers should move to the new paths
mixin.HumanMixin, mixin.OAuthAccountMixin, and mixin.RefreshTokenMixin: applications should authenticate through SystemAuth and link local records by sf_principal_id
identity/security: Lockout.CheckAndRecord in favor of Begin
rls: EntHook.SetContextFromContext, ContextInjector, ConnWithRLS, NewConnWithRLS, and GetConnWithRLS, which cannot take effect outside a transaction

fixed.description: SCIM user and group listing panicked on every ascending sort, including the default order
The identity/oauth Fosite storage dropped any subject that was not a UUID; tokens and authorization codes now record the subject
CreateClient reported every constraint failure, such as a nonexistent owner, as ErrClientExists; it now does so only for a duplicate client ID
Federation sync no longer discards lookup errors, and a delete reports synced only for an identity that was never linked
rls.SetupTestTenant and SetupTestUser inserted into tables that no longer existed; they now create organizations, human principals, and principal memberships, and report cleanup failures
rls.SystemForgeTables named a table that no longer existed, so MigrateSystemForge failed; it now names sf_principal_memberships
identity/oauth.NewProvider panicked on construction because its storage no longer satisfied Fosite's interfaces; it now does, checked at compile time
identity/oauth never recorded a token family, so revoking refresh and access tokens had no effect; tokens record their request as the family and rotation retires the exchanged refresh token
SystemAuth failed to record client-assertion JWT IDs under foreign-key enforcement, breaking private_key_jwt client authentication and leaving assertions replayable
Changing a user's email through SCIM no longer keeps the previous address's verification
The marketplace, organization, and invite APIs panicked at registration because list filters used pointer query parameters
The simple provider denied every organization permission check, because its permission names did not match the ones it looked up
SpiceDB GetRole reported editors as non-members
A managed principal's first sign-in to a relying party failed for lack of a verified email
In-memory stores, password login, and federation sync could match or adopt a human by an empty email
Invite emails are matched case-insensitively
organization.Service.Create failed for an organization without a plan instead of defaulting to free
GetMembership reports a missing membership as organization.ErrMembershipNotFound

identity/credential reports failures to record a credential's use and corrupt stored hashes (ErrCorruptCredential) instead of discarding them, and CreatePassword no longer creates a second password when its lookup fails

identity/oauth's authorization code exchange always failed and its tokens lost their subject; its grant storage now delegates to SystemAuth's, enforcing PKCE and redirect URIs and detecting code replay and refresh-token reuse
A signup that failed after creating the user left an account with no organization whose email could not sign up again
principal type-specific updates changed shared fields before checking the type, and CreateAgent accepted a missing or inactive delegating principal
identity/oauth.NewAPI panicked on every call because the Fosite interceptor was added after routes
The federation lookup handler read its path parameter with net/http's PathValue, which chi does not populate
The memory rate-limit store panicked when used after Close, and discarded windows after a fixed hour whatever their period

documentation.description: ADRs live in `docs/design/adrs/` with an index of statuses, under a Design section in the docs nav; ADR-006 (organization lifecycle), ADR-007 (memberships and entitlements as claims), ADR-008 (resource-scoped collaborators, with rbac/rebac guidance) and ADR-009 (management is a relationship) are added
ADR-004 (retire legacy User; Principal as the sole identity root) and ADR-005 (managed principals and manager relationships), with specs for INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-007 and INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008
Identity, OAuth, integration, and getting-started documentation rewritten for the principal model; the schema reference is generated from the Ent schema
The service-accounts page states that the RFC 7523 JWT-bearer grant is not implemented; the migration guide states that only Argon2id password hashes can be imported
Resource servers accepting AI agents via AAuth
Managed principals guide, with the email exception, login token security, and base manager relations added to the users, account security, and authorization conventions docs

highlights.description: `identity/systemauthsvc`: embed SystemAuth in a host binary with config loading, production checks, migrations, client bootstrap and health
Production safety checks enforced by `systemauthsvc.New`, not only by the command
`Service.Metadata()` lets in-process relying parties skip network discovery
Configuration overrides apply before defaults and validation; SystemAuth configuration can be loaded from bytes

added.description: `Server.OpenIDConfiguration()` and `Server.Ready(ctx)` on the SystemAuth server
`identity/systemauthsvc` exported SystemAuth service setup for host binaries
`systemauth.DecodeConfig` and `DecodeConfigFile` decode configuration without validating
`systemauthsvc.LoadConfigBytes`; `LoadConfig` validates after overrides

changed.description: `cmd/systemauth` builds the server through `systemauthsvc`; flags and defaults unchanged, production-refusal message reworded

documentation.description: Verified email design: ADR-003 and INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-006
Embedding SystemAuth in a host binary
